title: Develop a conversational search experience without rebuilding your app | ODSP922

segments.text: [ Music ]
GREG CRIST: Hey, everyone.
I'm Greg Crist, Cloud Ecosystem Architect here at Elastic.
I'm really excited to introduce this demo
from my colleague Jonathan Simon today.
Before we jump in, I want to set some context because what you're
about to see sits at the intersection of two things
that are moving incredibly fast right now:
the Microsoft AI ecosystem and Elastic's ability
to bring your own data into the AI conversation.
If you've been following what Microsoft's been building
with Azure OpenAI and Foundry IQ,
you know that developers now have a generally powerful,
integrated environment for discovering, evaluating,
deploying large language models.
That's a big deal.
But a model without the right context,
without the right data is just a very expensive autocomplete.
And that's where Elastic comes in.
Elastic is natively available on the Azure Marketplace, deployed,
managed and built through your Microsoft Marketplace.
It means you can go from zero
to production grade AI search deployment
without leaving the Azure ecosystem,
without a separate procurement motion,
and without managing additional vendor relationships.
It's Elastic on Azure, the way Azure customers expect things
to work.
When you pair Elastic with the models you've already exploring
in Microsoft Foundry model catalog,
whether it's Azure OpenAI or other models
from the broader catalog, you get something very compelling:
grounded, relevant, trustworthy AI answers that are powered
by your data and not just the model's training data,
which brings me to what Jonathan is going to show you today.
In his demo, you'll see how Elastics Agent Builder lets you
take a traditional e-commerce search experience
and transform it into a conversational AI agent.
One that understands your product catalog,
speaks your customers' language and delivers results
that actually drive conversation.
No full application rebuild required.
He'll walk through how to connect an LLM,
wire in your own data and deploy an agent that's ready
for your e-commerce site.
It's a practical look at what's possible
when you combine the best of Microsoft's AI platform
with Elastics context engineering
and search retrieval capabilities.
All right, over to you Jonathan.
JONATHAN SIMON: Thank you for that introduction.
Hello everyone, I'm Jonathan Simon.
I'm a Senior Product Marketing Engineer at Elastic
and today I'm going to show you how you can use Elastic Agent
Builder and workflows to create an AI search experience.
The agenda for this webinar is that I'll start
with a quick overview of the Elastic solutions
that are available, and then I'll introduce Agent Builder,
and then we'll jump right into a demo
where I'll show you a e-commerce website
for a fictitious company called Wayfinder Supply Company,
and then we'll look at Elastic Agent Builder.
I'll give you an overview of that.
We will use Agent Builder to create a workflow.
We'll create an MCP tool.
Then we'll create an agent, and then we'll integrate that agent
that we created back into the Wayfinder web app.
And then we'll conclude with a walkthrough of the architecture
that the Wayfinder web app is created with.
Okay. Elastic has three solutions: search,
observability and security.
Elasticsearch allows you to bring any data
into the Elasticsearch platform
and it gives you blazing fast lexical, exact match search,
semantic search based on vectors,
and now agentic search powered by AI agents created
with Elastic Agent Builder.
Elastic Observability is if you need observability
into the applications that you're running.
So, if you need application performance monitoring, metrics
and more, all you have to do is bring your logs into Elastic
and we'll use AI to parse and partition those logs
into a structured format that will allow you
to see instantly exactly what's going on in your applications.
Elastic Security.
If you've been tasked with protecting systems
or monitoring endpoints, or even running a security operations
center, Elastic Security has features like attack discovery,
automatic remediation with workflows that will enable you
to stay ahead of the modern cybersecurity threats
that are ever present.
Now, to get started with Elastic,
Azure is a great place to do that.
All you have to do is log into Azure,
go to the Microsoft Marketplace and search
for Elastic Serverless
and you'll see the three solutions pop up.
Then all you have to do is click "Get it Now"
and that will create a full featured Elastic project
that you can get started with.
And now I'm proud to announce Elastic Agent Builder.
It's been available in technical preview for a while now,
but it is officially generally available so you can use it
for your production workloads.
Now, the best way to explain how Elastic Agent Builder works is
to show you.
So, let me do that right now with a demo.
All right, so this is an e-commerce website
that sells camping gear for a company called Wayfinder.
Now, all of the products, descriptions,
the titles that you'll see we created with generative AI.
And the search for this website is powered by Elastic.
So, let's check it out.
We can browse gear and you can see, you can click an item,
see its images, see its details, its title, you can add it
to cart, all the things that you'd expect
with an e-commerce website and there's also search.
So, let's check that out.
You can see we've got chat-based search, we've got hybrid search,
we've got lexical search.
So, let's go ahead and try a query.
What if I typed "jackets?"
And there we go.
We get a nice list of jackets to choose from.
But what if I were to type "coats?"
No results.
And that's because none of the products have the word "coat"
or "coats" in their title or their descriptions.
What if I try hybrid search?
There we go, we get jackets again.
And that's because we have run the titles and descriptions
through the Elastic Inference Service to create vectors
and store those in a vector database.
And so, that hybrid search knows that coats are similar
to jackets and we get similar results
that we saw before for lexical search.
Now, suppose we wanted to get more sophisticated.
We wanted to actually create a trip planner that was powered
by AI that you could ask a question like this,
"Plan a three-day backpacking trip to Yosemite next weekend."
Let's run that.
And oh, "Trip Planner Agent is not built yet."
Well, that's okay, we can fix that.
Let's go build an agent to power the trip planner.
We can do that in Elastic Agent Builder.
Okay, so here is Elastic
and this is the Elastic Agent Builder interface.
The first thing that you should notice is
that we already have an agent that's enabled
and we have an LLM that the agent can use.
Now, this is configured right out of the box.
You don't have to do anything.
As soon as you install Elastic, this is available.
The other cool thing here to note is
that if I click this LLM, currently, it's Anthropic,
but you can see there's a whole bunch of other LLMs
that are preconfigured by default.
Now, suppose there was an LLM you wanted to use
that wasn't included in this list.
Well, Agent Builder has a solution for that, too.
We can click "Manage" and you can see all the pre-configured
LLMs here.
And then I can click "Create Connector."
We can search for Azure and select Azure.
And now, we need a place that we can find LLMs,
deploy LLMs and run LLMs.
Well, it turns out that there's a great place
to do that right in Azure.
So, I'm going to jump over to that right now.
This is the Microsoft Foundry running in Azure.
You can see we don't have any models deployed,
so let's go deploy one.
I'll click "Deploy Base Model" and you can see there's a ton
of different models to choose from.
Let's try "Mistral."
I'll select the "Mistral Large"
and let's go ahead and deploy that.
We can use the default settings.
There we go.
That was pretty fast.
We'll jump over to "Details," select the target URI,
we'll go back to the connector settings here and I'll plug
in that URI I just copied,
go back to the foundry and grab the key.
And enter the API key for authentication.
And then we'll give this connector a name.
We'll say "Mistral Large 3"
and then we'll click "Save and Test."
That saved the settings.
And then, now we have a nice interface to actually test it
out with a Hello World prompt.
So, we'll run that and there we go.
The test was successful.
So, now when we go back to Agent Builder
and we click the LLM selector,
we now see we've got Mistral Large 3.
So, right out of the box, Agent Builder is a great place for you
to try out agents with LLMs and your own data.
Okay, so now let's get on with building an agent
for the trip planner for that Wayfinder Supply Company web app
that you saw earlier.
The first thing we're going to need is a workflow.
So, I'll click "Workflows."
You can see, there's a few there already,
but we'll create a new one.
And now, I'm going to jump over to Visual Studio Code
to copy a workflow that I've got saved here.
And copy that.
Go back to the workflow and paste that in.
And let's quickly walk through the elements here
in this workflow.
So, you can see there's a version.
It's got a name.
Get customer profile.
There's an input.
It takes a user ID input.
That's a string, and this workflow is triggered manually.
There's a couple other ways that workflows can be triggered.
And workflows have one or more steps.
This one has a single step.
It's called Call CRM MCP.
And this is basically doing an HTP post call
to an external MCP server to get the customer profile.
Another cool thing about workflows is
that each step can have an on-failure handler.
And in this case, if there's a failure,
you can see that we'll retry twice.
And that you can add delays, too.
Here's a one-second delay between the retry attempts.
And then finally, workflows have the ability to log their output.
And so, in this case, we're doing a log to profile
and log profile to the console.
And so, that should take the results that we get
from running this workflow and create a log for it.
So, let's go ahead and save that and we'll run it.
And so, you can see we get this input for the User ID,
and we have the option to enter a value for that.
So, for this, I'll type "User Member."
I'll run it.
There we go.
Successful.
You can see the details of the response that came back.
And here's that log profile output
that I talked about earlier.
If I click that, we can see.
In a nice readable format,
we got a customer called Alex Hiker.
You can see his loyalty tier, lifetime purchases
and his lifetime value and his purchase history.
Cool. So, our workflow is working.
Great. All right, so now let's go and create a tool
that uses that workflow.
I'll go back to Agent Builder, click the "More" menu,
click "View All Tools," click "New Tool."
And here we can see there are different tool types.
There's an ESQL tool type, which is Elasticsearch query language,
which is similar to SQL, but even more powerful.
There is an index search tool type.
So, if you want to just do a straight search
against an Elastic index.
There's a Word workflow tool type,
which is what we'll be using.
And there's an MCP tool type which is currently
in Tech Preview, but that allows you to chain tools together
to create a complex workflow.
So, I'm going to go back to "Workflow"
and then we'll select the workflow that we just created,
the "Get Customer Profile" workflow,
and then we'll give this a Tool ID.
I'll jump back over to Visual Studio code, copy this Tool ID.
We'll call it Tool Workflow, Get Customer Profile, go back
and copy the description, and that's all we need.
I'll go ahead and click, "Save and Test."
So, that saved the details.
And then it opens this testing flyout.
Because it's using that workflow that took a input of User ID,
this tool that uses that workflow also needs the input.
And so, I'm going to type same thing I did before.
"User Menu, User Member," click "Submit."
And there we go, successful response.
And if we look at the output, it should be similar
to what we saw before.
And there he is, Alex Hiker, same customer, the loyalty tier,
lifetime value and the purchase history.
Sweet. Okay, so now we've got a tool that's using the workflow.
So, let's go ahead and create an agent
that will use that same tool.
One final thing I'll note about any tool that you create
in Agent Builder, it's officially an MCP tool.
So, with an API key, you can access that tool
from any other application that you're building.
Great. Okay, so we'll go to "Agents," I'll click "More,"
"View all Agents," and we're going to create a new agent.
I've got Visual Studio ready
with some values here that I can copy.
So, I'm going to copy this Agent ID.
We'll call this the "Trip Planner Agent."
We're going to copy these custom instructions.
Now, this isn't marked down.
That specifies exactly how you want the agent to behave.
In our case, we're telling it to search the product catalog
to generate a trip plan and all --
and the areas that it should be searching in for trip plans
and additional details.
Other items that we need are a display name.
So, I'll copy that.
We'll call this the Trip Planner Agent.
Need a description.
And that's all the details we need for our agent.
The final thing that we need to do though is
to assign it some tools.
And so, I will go ahead and click the Tools tab here
and then we'll sort by ID, and there is the tool
that we just created, the tool workflow,
"Get Customer Profile" tool.
So, I'll enable that and I will also enable these three tools.
Great. Now, I'll click Save and Chat."
And so, here we are, back in the Agent Builder interface.
And notice that now the agent that's selected is the Trip
Planner agent that we just created,
so that we can quickly test it out.
If you wanted to go back to a different agent,
you can simply click that
and then you got your options for different agents.
So, let's go ahead and test this.
I've got a prompt that we can test it with right here.
We can say, "Plan a three-day backpacking trip
to Yosemite this weekend," and we'll run that.
And one of the cool things about Agent Builder is
that it gives you a summary of what it's thinking and reasoning
about as it responds to your prompt.
You can also expand this section to see the exact steps
that it's taking as it does its reasoning.
So, you can see that it is planning a trip.
It knows that this weekend is March 13th through the 15th.
It's getting the weather conditions
for that and the road alerts.
It ran an ESQP query to get information
about the user's past click stream.
Now, it's searching for waterproof tents here.
Looking for rain Jackets.
Getting more details about the tent.
Looking for sleeping bags that are suitable
for the temperatures that are expected this weekend.
Getting more details about the sleeping bag.
And there we go.
Voila. We've got a backpacking trip itinerary
to Yosemite for this weekend.
You can see, it's got a trip overview,
it's got weather conditions, it's got product recommendations
that are suitable for the conditions of the trip timing,
and it's got a suggested three-day itinerary.
Sweet. So, we have an agent that we can now go and integrate back
with the Wayfinder web app so that we can get
that Trip Planner button working as it should be.
There's one final thing though that I wanted to show you
and that's the fact that any agent that you build
with Elastic Agent Builder,
its operations are also accessible via API.
So, it's cool that we can come in here into Agent Builder
and chat with it using this interface.
But even cooler is all of these functions are accessible
via API.
So, if you want to integrate
that into your existing apps, it's easy to do.
And so, for example, I can propose a query like this.
I could go look at the documentation for the APIs
for agents and I encourage you to do that.
But I wanted to show you how you can also just ask a question
like this.
"Hey, generate an example Python API call
to the Trip Planner agent with the prompt that we ran before."
And so, I'm showing you this because I want you to understand
that you can work with the agent
to help you generate example code
that will then help you get started
with integrating the agent into your existing apps.
And here we go.
Let me zoom in on this a bit.
Very simple Python.
It imports a request library.
It's got the URL to get to the agent.
It shows you that you're going to need an API key.
Here's the prompt that we ran.
It does the query and prints out the response.
Sweet. All right, so now we have everything that we need
to integrate this agent back into the Wayfinder web app.
So, let's go take a look at that.
I'm going to refresh.
Sweet. Okay, so let's give it a try.
Now, the way this app is written is such that
if the Trip Planner agent is available,
it will work as expected.
If it's not, you'll see the error message
that we saw before, that it's not yet implemented.
But because we just created the Trip Finder agent,
this should work.
Let's try it out.
We click "Trip Planner."
We'll click the suggested prompt here.
We'll say "This weekend" and run it.
All right, looks like it's working.
Now, similar to the Elastic Builder --
Elastic Agent Builder UI, this also shows the reasoning.
So, we can expand this section, and we can see
that it's planning a trip for Yosemite for this weekend.
It's getting the customer profile.
Looking for waterproof rain gear based on the temperature
that are expected this weekend.
Looking for sleeping bags that are suitable
for the temperatures expected this weekend.
Searching for backpacks, searching for tents.
All right, there we go.
That looks great.
Sweet. So, similar to what we saw before inside
of Agent Builder, now you can see it integrated right
into this web app.
So, we've got our three-day Yosemite backpacking trip plan
for this weekend.
You see the weather conditions.
We got recommended gear.
And look over here in this pane, you can see all the gear
that it's recommended with easy buttons to add it
to your shopping cart if you want to add that.
And then we also have a way to view the itinerary
which you can print out and bring with you on the trip.
So, that's pretty cool.
We went from an e-commerce site that had chat,
hybrid and lexical search to using Agent Builder
to build an agent that powered a concierge type trip planner
with product recommendations using Agent Builder and tied
to an LLM that's running on Microsoft Foundry.
Super powerful.
And let's do a quick tour of the architecture
that powers the Wayfinder web app.
So, starting at the top here you can see the front end is written
in React.
So, a user submits a query like "Plan my trip to Yosemite."
That sends an HTP request to the backend which is written
in Python running Fast API Server.
That Python backend does an API query
to the Elastic stack running the Trip Planner agent
that we just created.
And you can see that the Agent Builder agent has access
to the four tools that we gave it.
And starting over on this side,
you can see the Agent Builder has a tool called
"Product Search" that does semantic search
against the product catalog.
It also has a tool called "Get User Affinity"
which does an ESQL query to the user's clickstream.
Additionally, it has a tool called "Check Trip Safety"
and that goes through a workflow that does an HTP post
to an MCP server to get weather information.
And finally, the tool that we created, "Get Customer Profile,"
goes through a workflow called "Get Customer Profile"
that does an HTP post to an external MCP server
that queries a CRM service.
And all of that creates the trip planner that you just saw.
Hopefully, I've enticed you to check out Elastic
and Elastic Agent Builder and here are some resources
to help you get started.
The first one is the Agent Builder documentation,
and the next link here is a link to the GitHub repo
where you can find all the code you need
to run the Wayfinder Supply web app on your own machine.
It's also got a great readme
to explain exactly how everything works
and to help you get started.
Additionally, it's got a link to a workshop
that you can run completely for free without installing anything
to try it out yourself.
And finally, here's a QR code that you can scan
so that you can get Elastic running
on Azure free for seven days.
So, go ahead.
Give it a try.
GREG CRIST: Thanks, Jonathan.
That was a great practical walkthrough of how
to build an agent using Elastic as well
as the Microsoft Foundry environment.
If you'd like to learn more, please come visit Elastic
at the Microsoft Build Conference 2026
and use this QR code to learn more.
Thanks very much for your time today.
[ Music ]
